38:T1191,## Why

The account-pool broker HTTP surface was unreachable in production. `account-pool-broker-routes.ts` declared `ROUTE_PREFIX = "/internal/account-pool/v1"`, but the compat dispatcher only reaches `handleInternalWakeRoute` (which delegates to `handleAccountPoolBrokerRoute`) for `/api/internal/*` paths, and the router never strips `/api`. The two conditions can never both hold:

- to be dispatched to the handler at all, the path must start with `/api/internal/`
- to match `ROUTE_PREFIX`, it must start with `/internal/account-pool/v1`

So every broker route was dead code. A lease request to the canonical `/api/internal/account-pool/v1/lease` fell through to the generic `/api/internal/` device-secret auth and got `401 {"error":"Unauthorized"}` (note the shape: NOT the broker's own `{"ok":false,"error":"unauthorized"}` — that shape difference is how this was diagnosed). Fail-closed pool proxies translate that 401 into `503 "Account broker unavailable before upstream request"` on every single completion.

**Local repro evidence (2026-08-05):** this took down an entire local account pool — every session erroring with instant 503s (~10ms, i.e. failing at the lease step before any upstream call). Path probing pinned it:

```
POST /api/internal/account-pool/v1/lease -> 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"}   (generic /api auth)
POST /internal/account-pool/v1/lease     -> 404 {"error":"Not found"}      (not routed at all)
```

Ruled out along the way: lease exhaustion (restarts didn't help), token mismatch (proxy token == backend secret byte-for-byte), env not loading (running process had ENABLED=1 + correct SECRET), orphan process on the port. Applying this one-line prefix fix and restarting: broker health 200 with a real snapshot, 3/3 end-to-end completions through the proxy. Full diagnosis receipt: workspace `POOL-503-ROOTCAUSE-FIX-2026-08-05.md`.

## Fix

`ROUTE_PREFIX` -> `/api/internal/account-pool/v1`, matching the path the pool proxy actually calls and the only prefix the dispatcher can deliver. Direct-call tests and the consumer-metering doc updated to the canonical path. Comment added at the constant explaining why `/api` is load-bearing.

## Why existing tests missed it (production-path gap)

The existing suites (`account-pool-broker-routes.test.ts`, the delegation test in `internal-routes.test.ts`) invoke `handleAccountPoolBrokerRoute` / `handleInternalWakeRoute` **directly** with whatever path the fixture chooses — the same un-prefixed path the handler declared. Handler and tests agreed with each other while both disagreed with production routing, so the suite stayed green while the route was unreachable. That is exactly the gap that let this ship.

## Bidirectional test

New `account-pool-broker-routes.dispatch.test.ts` drives the REAL dispatcher entrypoint (`handleElizaCompatRoute` -> compat route chain -> `handleInternalWakeRoute` -> broker) with `/api/internal/account-pool/v1/*` from a loopback peer:

- `GET .../health` returns the broker health snapshot (200, `{ok:true,enabled:true}`)
- `POST .../lease` returns a real lease (accountId + accessToken, no refresh token echoed)
- wrong bearer gets the broker's own 401 shape `{ok:false,error:"unauthorized"}`, not generic auth's `{"error":"Unauthorized"}` — pinning the exact discriminator used to diagnose the outage

**Verified both directions:** with `ROUTE_PREFIX` reverted to the old un-prefixed value, all 3 dispatch tests fail (handler never reached); with the fix, all pass.

Also isolates the `internal-routes.test.ts` broker-delegation test into a scratch `ELIZA_HOME`/`ELIZA_STATE_DIR`: broker health enumerates real accounts, and without isolation that test read (and failed to decrypt) the developer's actual account vault.

## Consumers checked

Grepped the tree for `/internal/account-pool` — the only un-prefixed references were the handler constant itself, the direct-call tests, and the metering doc (all updated here). The pool-proxy side already calls the `/api`-prefixed path, so no consumer depends on the old prefix (it never worked).

## Verification

- vitest: `account-pool-broker-routes.dispatch.test.ts` + `account-pool-broker-routes.test.ts` + `internal-routes.test.ts` + `route-auth-policy.dispatch.test.ts` + `route-auth-policy.test.ts` — 43/43 pass
- `tsc --noEmit` — no new errors in touched files (remaining errors are pre-existing unbuilt-sibling-package imports: plugin-meetings, cloud-routing)

Closes #17840

## What was wrong

The service has been unbuildable since **2026-06-28**. Its Dockerfile builds from the service directory:

```dockerfile
COPY package.json ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --production
```

and `a07084e9cbc` added `@elizaos/cloud-services-common` to its dependencies. `workspace:*` has nothing to resolve against in a context containing only this package. Reproduced by running that exact step:

```
error: Workspace dependency "@elizaos/cloud-services-common" not found
error: @elizaos/cloud-services-common@workspace:* failed to resolve
```

**Two things kept it quiet.** Nothing builds this service — no repo trigger on Railway (`repoTriggers: NONE`, `source: null`) and a single `test` job in its workflow. And the service ships its own `bun.lock` written before the dependency existed, pinning `hono@4.12.18` against a manifest asking for `4.12.34`. So `--frozen-lockfile` was reading a lockfile that could never have installed the thing that was missing.

## What it cost

The production image dates from **2026-05-14** — the last build that could succeed. Everything since is a redeploy of that image. The running container still logs the pre-#17746 error string, which is how this surfaced:

```
[ERRO] Background message processing failed
       error="Identity resolve response missing userId, organizationId, or agentId"
```

#17746 and #17764 both fix connector onboarding for every linked user. Both merged. Neither has ever run in production. No test, typecheck or lint could have caught it, because none of them builds the image.

## The fix

Build context is the repository root. The deps stage writes a pruned workspace root containing only this service and the package it needs, so the workspace link resolves without installing the monorepo.

The stale service lockfile is **deleted rather than regenerated**: this is a workspace member and the root lockfile is authoritative for it — and the root lockfile already has both packages and the right `hono`.

Nothing guards the deploy half. A service can go months without a successful build and nothing says so — that is what happened here. Refs #17866

## What this fixes

Shared-tier agents run container-free in the hosted shared runtime — their `node_id`/`container_name` are NULL by design, and the heartbeat sweep excludes the tier for exactly that reason. Before that design landed, shared agents got real containers, and **six rows from that era still carry their placement**. Their containers are long gone (the orphan reconciler reaped them), but the rows still count toward node allocation, since `running` is non-terminal — and nothing can ever collect them:

- the heartbeat never dials the `shared` tier;
- the warm-pool reconcilers only see pool rows;
- the orphan reconciler starts from the Docker listing, so a row whose container is absent is structurally unreachable.

Measured on production 2026-08-06: **exactly six rows**, each with its last heartbeat 26 days old, **zero created in the last 14 days**. A remnant of the pre-container-free design, not an active leak — so this is a data migration with no code change. It releases the same column set as `executeSleep`, the canonical release shape, and the rows become ordinary container-free shared agents. `total_billed` on all six is 0.00; nothing was ever charged for the phantom placement.

## Scope guards — each load-bearing, each mutation-tested

| guard | protects | removing it turns red |
|---|---|---|
| `pool_status IS NULL` | warm-pool rows are shared-tier AND legitimately placed while unclaimed | ✔ 1 fail |
| `status = 'running'` | `deletion_pending`/`deletion_failed` keep their locator for the delete-retry sweep | ✔ 1 fail |
| `execution_tier = 'shared'` | dedicated tiers, whatever their heartbeat says | ✔ 1 fail |
| heartbeat stale > 7 days | a placed shared row with a recent beat would be live evidence the container-free assumption is wrong somewhere — left for a human, not erased | ✔ 1 fail |

Proven on a real PGlite table with one fixture row per boundary: 6 pass / 0 fail at baseline, and each guard's removal fails exactly one pin.

## Numbering note

The migration is `0190`, deliberately skipping `0189`, which is claimed by the open lifecycle-revision PR (#17830) — the two branches must not collide on a journal index. `drizzle-kit check` passes on this journal.

# Part 1 — IAC v2 test contract (supersedes #17825)

Commit 4fa232298f6 (#17805) bumped `INFERENCE_AUTH_CONTEXT_VERSION` 1→2 and reshaped the inference auth/admission surface without updating the tests that pin the old contract — the matrix has been deterministically red at every sha since (certification runs 31073689058 and forensics on its signed bundle). Seven test files updated to the v2 contract; **assertions strengthened, never weakened**:

- v1 records now have an explicit REJECTED case of their own (shape guard + pending-charge `v`)
- the hot-path benchmark counts the two new cold-path loads (`loadInferenceAdmissionSnapshot`, `loadInferenceAppKeyScope`): cold = 1 each, warm = 0
- the retired per-route native Cloudflare gates are asserted **never consulted** even when present-and-denying; rate policy is asserted to ride the admission snapshot via `enforceOrgRateLimit`
- the a2a trust-boundary integration runs the cache-enabled Worker lane with `executionCtx` on every request — production's actual lane — instead of the compatibility lane

All 5 previously-truncated cloud-api failures reproduced and traced to this same bump; none had a different root cause.

Found-not-fixed (pre-existing, reported for a follow-up): `trackApiKeyUsage` (`workers-hono-auth.ts:108`) reads `c.executionCtx` whose Hono getter THROWS on contexts without one — the `?.waitUntil` guard never runs, so bare-Hono API-key requests 500. Present since the v2.0.4 baseline.

# Part 2 — apps memory-cache eviction (supersedes #17829)

Fifth (and per current forensics, final) at-sha matrix red on develop. #17805 put a worker-lifetime `InMemoryLRUCache` in front of `appsService.getById`, but the repository's `invalidateAppCacheEntries` only deletes shared-cache keys — after `update`/`delete`, a same-worker read returns the **pre-mutation row for up to the 30s TTL**. `apps.test.ts` pins exactly that eviction contract and has been red at every sha since (the robot certification never reached it: its cloud-shared lane stopped at batch 23 on the billing failure fixed in #17825; this was next in line).

This is a real production staleness bug, not just a test skew: dashboard edits and deletes could read back stale for the TTL window on the same worker.

Fix: the memory cache moves to its own module (`inference-app-memory-cache.ts`) so the repository can evict without a service↔repository import cycle; `invalidateAppCacheEntries` now evicts it on every persisting mutation.

Closes #17866

## What was wrong

`WarmPoolManager.healthCheck()` is the only thing in the tree that probes a **ready** warm-pool entry and collects it when its container is gone. It had no live caller — the only one was `/api/v1/cron/pool-health-check` on the container-control-plane, which this daemon's own comments call deprecated.

This is the same omission as `replenish`, documented fifteen lines away in the same file, with a worse consequence: **nothing else can see those rows.**

- The heartbeat skips them. `listRunning()` filters `execution_tier != 'shared'`, and `createPoolEntry` never sets the tier, so every pool row falls to the schema default `shared` — while holding a real `node_id` and `container_name`. The docblock's premise, that shared rows are container-free by design, is simply false for pool rows.
- `reconcileUnclaimable` cannot reach them: its candidate query ends `NOT (warmPoolRuntimeReadyConditions)`, and these rows *are* ready.
- The orphan reconciler cannot reach them: it starts from the Docker listing, so an empty node yields an empty candidate set.

A ready pool entry whose container died therefore stayed `running` forever. `running` is not terminal, so it counts toward the node's allocation, and `findDrainCandidates` refuses any node with `allocated > 0` — a row is treated as proof of a workload. **The node can never be drained.**

## What it cost

Measured on production 2026-08-06 by diffing `docker ps -a` on all nine nodes against the rows that claim them:

| | |
|---|---|
| real agent containers | 169 |
| rows claiming a container | 238 |
| **rows claiming a container that does not exist** | **77** |

Three autoscaled ccx33 bought on 26, 27 and 28 July hold four such rows each, have **zero containers**, and have read as fully allocated for ten days. `syncAllocatedCounts` re-asserts that count every five minutes, and the billing crons select on `status = 'running'` with no node-side check — so those rows are billed hourly.

## The change

One phase, wired between drain and replenish: after drain so it does not probe entries just removed, before replenish so the refill sizes itself against the depth left once dead entries are collected.

This does not give `healthCheck()` new power — it was written to destroy dead entries and ran that way through the control-plane. It puts it back in service.

## Evidence

<details>
<summary>Tests — each pin mutation-verified</summary>

| pin | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| the infra cycle drives `healthCheck` and maps the collected count | remove the phase (= develop) | 1 fail |
| it runs after drain and before replenish | move it after replenish | 1 fail |
| a probe failure propagates instead of reporting a healthy pool | swallow it into a zero result | 1 fail |

```
provisioning-worker.pool-health      4 pass  0 fail
provisioning-worker                 51 pass  0 fail
provisioning-worker.replenish        3 pass  0 fail
provisioning-worker.backup-verify    2 pass  0 fail
```

`provisioning-worker.image-rollout` fails 1 of 3 identically with this change stashed — a pre-existing `@elizaos/core` resolution failure in this worktree, unrelated to the diff.

</details>

## Deliberately not in this PR

**The 77 rows already stranded.** Cleaning them needs the reverse reconciler — "row claims container C on node N, `docker ps` does not list it past a grace window → release the placement". No such path exists today: every writer that NULLs `node_id`/`container_name` (`executeSleep`, `retireFailedWarmClaimForRetry`, `trySetProvisioning`) is triggered by a job or an error string, never by container absence. That is a new subsystem mutating production rows and deserves its own review. **This PR stops producing them.**

**`shutdown` / `executeSuspend` keep their placement** after removing the container, which is a real asymmetry against `executeSleep`. It costs no capacity — `stopped` is terminal for both the allocation and the retention count — so fixing it here would be a behaviour change to the suspend/resume path with no measured problem behind it.

**Arming `ORPHAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED`** (it issues `docker rm -f`) and the node `capacity` values (the autoscaler declares ccx33 as 4 slots while the original nodes declared 24 carry 38) are ops decisions, listed in the issue.

# Risks

Low. Native clients defensively remove remote JS/frame entries that platform policy already prohibits; web and desktop behavior is unchanged. Calendar's Google error classes move to the Workspace package's existing dependency-light `calendar` subpath (type imports stay on the root barrel, erased at compile time).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Ports the still-applicable slices of #17596 onto the post-refactor develop tree. Shaw's plugin-surface consolidation (`6c25cf6d339`) split `plugin-simple-views` into `plugin-notes` and deleted the duplicate simple-calendar in favor of `plugin-calendar`'s CalendarView, which **already fixed** the original PR's largest slice (the default-profile registration gap). Two independent production boundaries from #17596 still reproduce on develop head and are fixed here:

- **Native view catalog policy (`packages/ui`):** the agent route filters dynamic views using `X-Eliza-Platform`, but a live phone gateway can omit the header and return the unfiltered registry, leaking `bundleUrl`/`frameUrl` entries (e.g. Notes) to restricted native clients. The renderer then selected `DynamicViewLoader` for ids whose signed in-process registrations should have won, dead-ending on `ViewRestrictedState`. Fix is two defense-in-depth boundaries: `fetchViewList` strips remote JavaScript/frame entries on iOS/Android before the app-shell merge, and `renderViewRouterContent` prefers an exact signed app-shell registration over a stale remote-bundle registry snapshot on restricted platforms only. Web/desktop keep remote bundles and remote-bundle precedence.
- **Calendar import isolation (`plugins/plugin-calendar`):** `CalendarService` imported two runtime error classes from the `@elizaos/plugin-google-workspace` root barrel. Importing Calendar therefore evaluated the Workspace SDK graph (client-factory eagerly imports `googleapis`) and aborted plugin import on production images without the optional SDK, before the local calendar view could register. Runtime values now come from the dependency-light `@elizaos/plugin-google-workspace/calendar` subpath; the root import is type-only.

## What was NOT carried forward (superseded by the refactor)

- `MOBILE_VIEW_PLUGINS` / optional-plugin-import registration of `plugin-simple-views`: the package no longer exists. `plugin-notes` is in `LEAN_CHAT_PLUGINS` + `RUNTIME_APP_PLUGIN_SUBPATHS`, and calendar is owned by `plugin-calendar` with its signed `CalendarView`.
- `shared-nav-targets` `calendar → simple-calendar` translation and the `views-show.ts` matcher-namespace fallback: develop's `calendar` matcher id now equals the live view id (`plugin-calendar` registers `id: "calendar"`), so the namespace split this compensated for is gone.
- The simple-views production-path Playwright spec: exercises deleted surfaces.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix, non-breaking.

# Testing

## Develop-red proof (both slices, on this branch's base)

1. **Calendar import boundary:** on develop head, booting `calendarPlugin` under a loader that rejects `googleapis` aborts with `googleapis must not be evaluated while Calendar boots` before the view registers. With the fix the plugin loads and `views[calendar].componentExport === "CalendarView"`.
2. **Native catalog policy:** stashing the two UI fixes while keeping the new expectations fails 3/3 targeted assertions (`enforceDynamicViewPolicy is not a function` x2; the signed-renderer test selects `DynamicViewLoader` instead of the signed component).

# Risks

Low, and additive. No existing lane changes what it runs: the agent package's default-lane exclusions are untouched, `test:remote-capabilities` is untouched, and the integration config gains one include glob rather than losing any. The new CI step matches no file on `develop` today, so it cannot turn a green run red on landing; it exists so the next suite is picked up without wiring.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

A `*.integration.test.ts` suite anywhere under `packages/agent` runs in **no CI lane**. Two independent holes combine to produce that:

**The package's own lanes exclude the suffix.** `packages/agent/vitest.config.ts:181` excludes `**/*.integration.test.{ts,tsx}` and `packages/agent/scripts/run-vitest-batches.mjs:21` excludes `/\.integration\.test\.[cm]?tsx?$/`. That is deliberate — those lanes have a weight budget — and this PR does not change it.

**Nothing re-includes them.** `packages/scripts/vitest/integration.config.ts` is the only lane that could, and:

1. Its include list covered `packages/agent/test/**/*.integration.test.ts` but had no `packages/agent/src/**` entry, even though it carries exactly that pair for plugins (`plugins/*/test/**` **and** `plugins/*/src/**`).
2. Both of its CI callers pass an explicit file list, which narrows the run regardless of the include globs — `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `plugin-personal-assistant`'s `test:integration` (three named files), and `lifeops-live-validation-11632.yml` names one. So even the `packages/agent/test/**` glob that *was* present has never selected a file in CI.

This is a repeat of a failure the config already documents twice in its own comments — "16 `*.integration.test.ts` files in `app-lifeops/test/` were dead in CI" and the scheduler suite that "was dead the same way."

The fix keeps discovery by pattern at every step:

- adds `packages/agent/src/**/*.integration.test.ts` to the integration config's include list, matching the existing `plugins/*/src/**` precedent;
- adds `packages/agent` a `test:integration` script that runs the repo integration config with a **path filter, not a file list**, so a new suite needs no edit anywhere;
- adds a CI step to the existing integration job, whose `if` gate already covers `packages/agent/**` via the `server` lane (`ci-path-gate.mjs:55`);
- adds a regression test asserting both agent roots stay covered, and failing if a suite ever appears under a third root.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking): restores CI coverage for a category of test that silently had none.

# Documentation changes needed?

Done in-PR: `packages/agent/CLAUDE.md` and its byte-identical `AGENTS.md` twin list the new command.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

Reproduce the gap directly. On `develop`, drop any file named `*.integration.test.ts` under `packages/agent/src/` and confirm neither `bun run --cwd packages/agent test` nor any CI lane executes it. Then on this head:

```bash
bun run --cwd packages/agent test:integration
```

## Detailed testing steps

The regression test is red on `develop`'s config and green on this head, and the probe run shows the same file being rejected by the default lane and picked up by the integration lane.

# What changed

The worker-lifetime app cache and its hydration generation now have one shared owner. Repository update/delete boundaries atomically invalidate that state before clearing external cache keys. A read that began before a mutation can no longer resume afterwards and republish its stale row into the process-local or shared cache.

The new real PGlite regression deliberately pauses `findById` after it captures the old row, performs a repository update, resumes the older hydration, and proves the stale row is not republished. A fresh service read then returns the updated Postgres row.

# Why this is narrower than the previous head

The previous head also carried seven IAC v2 test files. Those exact test semantics are now present on `develop`, and retaining them here would duplicate upstream work and preserve a review-blocked broad status assertion. This head changes four cache-ownership paths only and directly pins the stronger generation-fence invariant identified by the reviewer.

# Known gaps / failures

No known product failure on the exact head. GitHub CI is the authoritative clean-runner confirmation.47:T955,## Problem

`ElizaClient.connectWs()` carries a guard for Capacitor native builds, where the page origin is a synthetic bundle host (e.g. `https://localhost`) with no server behind it:

```ts
if (!this.baseUrl && typeof host === "string") {
  const hasPort = host.includes(":");
  const isLoopback = host.startsWith("127.") || host.startsWith("localhost:");
  if (!hasPort && !isLoopback) return;
}
```

The guard is **unconditional**: any client with no explicit `baseUrl`, served same-origin from a portless HTTPS host, silently never opens `/ws`. That is the standard self-hosted deployment shape (nginx terminating TLS on 443 in front of the agent server, UI served same-origin).

REST keeps working, so the breakage is invisible except that every server-pushed WS event is lost: `proactive-message` (proactive sends, voice-turn mirrors), `conversation-updated`, agent events. Live-pushed messages never render in the open chat thread until a manual reload.

Found live on a self-hosted deploy while QAing realtime voice: spoken turns were persisted server-side and mirrored over `proactive-message`, but the browser had no `/ws` socket at all, so the open thread stayed stale at every sheet detent.

## Fix

Gate the skip on `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` — the only environment where the origin host is genuinely synthetic. Plain browsers (including a Capacitor-built web bundle served over HTTP/HTTPS, where the `Capacitor` global has no native platform) keep the same-origin WebSocket. Probe failure reads as "not native", preserving the browser WS path.

## Tests

`packages/ui/src/api/client-base-websocket.test.ts`:
- **fails before / passes after**: `opens a same-origin websocket from a portless HTTPS host in a plain browser` — stubs `location` = `https://sol-dev.example.test` (no port), client with no baseUrl, asserts `wss://…/ws` is opened with the token param.
- native contract preserved: `still skips the synthetic-host websocket on Capacitor native` — same origin shape + `Capacitor.isNativePlatform() === true`, asserts no socket attempt.
- all 16 existing websocket-policy tests unchanged and green (18/18 total).

Also verified end-to-end on the live self-hosted deploy: after the fix the page opens `wss://<host>/ws`, and voice-turn `proactive-message` mirrors render live in the open thread (half and full detents, no duplicates, reconcile-by-id intact).48:Tf82,Any agent whose sandbox row points at a node that was later purged from `docker_nodes` can **never be deleted by its owner**: `hydrateContainerFromDb` throws `Missing persisted docker node metadata for node "..."`, `isIgnorableSandboxStopError` doesn't recognize the shape, and the delete escalates → retries 3x → lands in `deletion_failed` permanently.

Found live on staging tonight: agent `0b402068` (user-visible as "Provisioning permanently failed... / deletion failed") was undeletable through the platform until the dangling node pointer was cleared by hand; two other orgs' agents (`15bd4e15`, `25abaceb`) sit in `deletion_failed` from the same cause.

Fix: the missing-node-metadata shape joins the ignorable set for stop/delete teardown — the container's node no longer exists, so there is nothing to stop, and deletion proceeds to credential revocation + row delete. The predicate is consumed at exactly one call site (the `deleteAgent` phase-2 bounded-teardown classification), so the ignorable treatment is scoped to teardown by construction. Sibling hydration failures (missing hostname/port data) remain non-ignorable — pinned by a new negative test.

# Risks

Low, and narrowing rather than widening. No TTL, read path, or cache key changes. The only behavioral difference is that the repository-side invalidation now advances the hydration generation as the service-side one always has — so a read racing a mutation declines to publish instead of publishing a superseded row. The failure mode being removed is a stale publish; the fix cannot itself publish anything new.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`invalidateCache` in the apps service has always done two things: delete the memory entry **and** advance `appByIdHydrationGeneration`. That counter is load-bearing — `loadAndCacheAppById` samples it before its DB round trip and re-checks it afterwards, so a read that began before an invalidation notices and declines to publish the row it is holding.

When the repository gained its own eviction path, only the delete came with it:

```ts
export function evictInferenceAppMemoryCache(appId: string): void {
  inferenceAppMemoryCache.delete(appId);
}
```

The counter stayed private to `services/apps.ts`, so `invalidateAppCacheEntries` (`repositories/apps.ts:36`, reached from `:480`, `:496`, `:498` — each awaited after the write commits) evicted without bumping. That leaves this interleaving open:

1. A read enters `loadAndCacheAppById(id)`, samples `generation = 0`, awaits `findById(id)` → pre-mutation row **R**.
2. A mutation commits and invalidates. Generation is still `0`.
3. The read resumes, `0 !== 0` is false, and it publishes **R** into `cache.set(cacheKey, …)` *and* `inferenceAppMemoryCache.set(id, …)`.

The bug the evictor was added to fix stranded a stale row in one worker's memory for the 30s LRU TTL. This interleaving is worse: the row is republished into the **shared** cache, so the staleness escapes the worker and is served cluster-wide for the full `CacheTTL.app.byId`. It is also not exotic — `scheduleAppByIdHydration` runs hydrations in the background under `waitUntil`, so reads overlapping mutations are the steady state.

The fix moves the generation into `inference-app-memory-cache.ts` next to the cache it guards, and has the evictor do both halves. Evicting without bumping is no longer expressible, which is the actual defect — not either call site individually.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking): restores an invariant the service path already held.

# Documentation changes needed?

None. The module header now states why the two pieces of state live together.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

```bash
bun test packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/apps-inference-cache.test.ts
```

Then revert `evictInferenceAppMemoryCache` to a delete-only body and re-run — the new case fails, and nothing else does.

## Detailed testing steps

The test parks an authoritative read inside `findById` (waiting on `appReads` so the invalidation provably lands *after* the generation sample), invalidates through the repository primitive, releases the read, and asserts it did not republish into either cache.

4c:Tfa9,Every signed-out page load spams the console with `[LifeOpsActivitySignals] unexpected capture failure: ApiError: Unauthorized`, repeating on each 5-second readiness poll. Observed on the live staging deployment during tonight's smoke test (both origins, every anonymous page).

Cause: the capture's readiness probe hits `/api/status` on mount and every 5s; signed-out it rejects with `ApiError { kind: "http", status: 401 }`, and `isExpectedProbeFailure` only recognized network/timeout/503 — so the 401 fell through to `reportCaptureError` → `console.error`.

Fix (J4-style expected degrade, matching the module's existing classifier convention): a `isUnauthenticatedError` predicate (ApiError, http, 401) joins `isExpectedProbeFailure` — quiet stand-down, poll keeps checking so capture engages on the first post-sign-in poll — and `reportCaptureError`'s expected-shape early return, covering a session that expires between probe and signal send. Deliberately NOT auth-state gating: wiring React session state into this headless service would add cross-layer coupling the file avoids; and deliberately not a blanket catch — 500s, parse errors, and non-ApiError failures still surface as `capture_error` + console.error, preserved by the existing tests.

4d:T1475,Robot-pool certification run 31073689058 completed the **full matrix in ~78 minutes** (the capacity fix works) and honestly signed RED with 9 failing tasks. Forensics on the bundle classified every failure; this PR fixes the classes the runner environment owns:

- **(a) env contamination** — the production box's TTY/color vars leak ANSI codes into captured stderr, breaking the agent early-logs mirror suppression; and the runner env exposes a **real `ELIZA_VAULT_PASSPHRASE` to test processes** (security concern, flagged in a workflow comment for org-side review).
- **(b) machine capability** — vault's keychain tests need a D-Bus session bus, which hosted runners have and the robot service lacks (`isKeychainUnsafe()` branches on it). The brief's own hypothesis inverted honestly: the keychain was *bypassed*, not real.
- **(c) load timing** — noted, deliberately NOT band-aided with retries (5s/10s hooks on a box also running production workloads; if it persists post-sanitization the lever is scheduling, not retries).
- **(d) genuine at-sha regressions** — cloud-shared and a ui guard fail on ANY runner at that sha (fixed separately; sanitization must not hide them).

Change: a `Prepare hermetic runner` step (gated `inputs.runner == 'robot'`) builds an `env -i` wrapper — explicit allowlist (PATH, fresh HOME under RUNNER_TEMP, TMPDIR, TZ=UTC, LANG, CI, USER, GITHUB_*/RUNNER_*, and only the two chain secrets) — run under `dbus-run-session` for hosted parity. The scenario-lane and certify steps are prefixed with the wrapper; **the hosted path is byte-unchanged**. Everything else drops: the vault passphrase, POSTGRES_URL, TERM/FORCE_COLOR, ambient DBUS/XDG state.

53:T14d8,A turn-latency regression measured on a live agent: memory/recall turns took **33–56 seconds** where the previous release served the same store in ~2s.

## Root cause

`44e6088774e` (#17490, "make provider deadlines cancellation-safe") did two things: it declared explicit budgets for `relevant-conversations` (10s) and `recent-conversations` (8s), and it removed the **default** budget in `packages/core/src/runtime.ts` (`return 3_000` → `return undefined`). `rolodex` declares no budget, so it became unbounded.

`rolodex` awaits a relationships-graph snapshot. On a large store the cold rebuild issues thousands of queries against the in-process PGlite — WASM Postgres on the **main JS thread** — so while it runs, no I/O callback in the process can complete. The turn's model response had already arrived and sat unread in the socket.

The deleted default's own comment predicted this verbatim: *"Without an enforced deadline a provider doing synchronous network work can hold every message turn hostage for tens of seconds and still count as healthy."*

## Change

- **`rolodex` declares `timeoutMs: 3_000, timeoutMode: "degrade"`** — the same pattern #17490 applied to its siblings. Contact context is supplemental; degrading beats stalling. `degrade` is required because declared budgets default to `fail`, which would turn an overrun into a failed composition.
- **`getCachedModel` serves an expired snapshot immediately** and refreshes through the existing single-flight promise in the background; only the first-ever build (no snapshot at all) awaits. TTL 30s → 5min, since it now governs staleness rather than turn latency, and merge mutations still invalidate eagerly. A single observer logs rebuild failures and the last good snapshot is retained.

Also worth flagging for a follow-up (not in this diff): `CLOUD_ACCOUNT`, `elizacloud_credits`, `CLOUD_APPS`, `elizacloud_models` and `adminPanel` are likewise undeclared and unbounded since #17490.

Fixes #17862.

# What changed

- Treats one-to-one `VOICE_DM` as the same direct-addressed Stage-1 response surface as `DM`, `API`, and `SELF`.

- Proves direct-channel grammar cache reuse and group-voice separation.

This is provider-independent runtime behavior for the Cartesia Ink 2 -> Cerebras -> Cartesia Sonic 3.5 path. It contains no local ASR, VAD, Kokoro, or native audio implementation.

Fix: the memory cache moves to its own module (`inference-app-memory-cache.ts`) so the repository can evict without a service↔repository import cycle; `invalidateAppCacheEntries` now evicts it on every persisting mutation.

# Risks

The workflow change is routing-only on a `workflow_dispatch`-only surface: the `robot` choice now defers to `HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE` exactly like every other fleet route in the repository, and `hosted` behavior is byte-identical. # Background

## What does this PR do?

#17812 routed `certification-hosted.yml` to the `hetzner-robot` pool on the dispatch input alone:

```yaml
runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'robot' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","hetzner-robot"]') || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
```

Two consequences:

1. **`bun run verify` is red on `develop` for everyone.** `audit:hetzner-fleet-routing` allowlists exact, `HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE`-gated selectors and throws on anything else touching the fleet labels. The collector also flags the input's `description` scalar, which contained the literal label string.
2. **The behavioral gap the contract exists to prevent:** an operator dispatching `runner: robot` while the fleet is offline queues the run against zero registered runners indefinitely. #17812's "hosted stays the default" fail-safe covers only the default, not the explicit choice.

The fix composes the input **with** the gate, in the same shape as the contract's existing `PULL_REQUEST_HOSTED_SELECTOR`:

```yaml
runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.runner != 'robot' && '["ubuntu-24.04"]' || vars.HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE != 'true' && '["ubuntu-24.04"]' || '["self-hosted","hetzner-robot"]') }}
```

Truth table: `hosted` (or anything non-`robot`) → `ubuntu-24.04` always; `robot` + fleet online → the pool; `robot` + fleet offline/missing/false → `ubuntu-24.04`, never a stranded queue. That exact string is added to `DIRECT_RUNNER_SELECTORS` with a comment naming the workflow, why a dispatch input is a safe discriminator there, and the degrade guarantee. The description is reworded so prose no longer carries collector trigger substrings, with an inline comment explaining that constraint for the next editor.

Kept from #17812, untouched: the `runner` input itself, `timeout-minutes: 300`, and the run-31067341248 rationale.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking): restores the repository verify gate and the fleet fail-safe.

# Documentation changes needed?

None; the constraint is documented at both edit sites.

57:T124f,Live staging incident tonight, with a production landmine attached.

`prepareManagedElizaEnvironment` stamps `ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN: "1"` — a boolean platform flag — on every managed agent. Its NAME matches the `/TOKEN/` sensitivity pattern, so the Worker encrypts it at rest. But **no provisioning daemon in any environment holds `SECRETS_MASTER_KEY`** (the cloud-cf-deploy workflow never syncs it — it exists only as a wrangler.toml comment; the daemon deploy workflow's reconcile is skip-when-empty and the GH secret is unset for both environments). Result: every cold provision of an agent carrying the encrypted flag dies with:

```
Your cloud agent failed to start: Environment decryption failed:
Failed to decrypt agent environment variable ELIZA_ALLOW_WS_QUERY_TOKEN:
SECRETS_MASTER_KEY must be set for field encryption
```

Verified ground truth from both databases: the ONLY key ever encrypted is this flag (staging 27 rows, prod 26 rows — zero user BYO secrets affected). Staging failed live tonight for a real user; **prod shows zero failures only because nothing cold-provisioned recently — the next one fails identically.**

Fix: add the flag to `NEVER_ENCRYPT_ENV_KEYS`, the established escape hatch for platform-stamped non-secrets (`ELIZAOS_API_KEY` precedent), with the failure mode documented in a comment.

Data remediation (out of band, backed up): staging's 27 rows rewritten to plaintext and the lane verified recovered end-to-end (three agents reached `running` post-fix, including the affected user's). Prod's 26 rows get the same treatment.

Follow-ups worth their own issues (reported, not in this diff): the never-synced `SECRETS_MASTER_KEY` means real BYO-secret encryption is inert platform-wide; POST /eliza/agents does two bounded container pushes inline before responding (observed 15s+ client timeouts); the staging agent-lane worker box is SSH-unreachable with any held credential.

59:T10f3,Fourth live-run fix for the certification chain (#17792 → #17794 → #17796 → this). Run 31057802513 proved the scenario lane works — **226 artifacts ingested into the scenario-runner silo** — and still died at signing:

```text
scenario-runner          ingested  226
error [VERDICTS_INVALID]: invalid verdicts document (...-verdicts.json):
verdicts: Too small: expected array to have >=1 items
```

Root cause: the manual `bundle:create → certify:rollup → certify:sign` chain (inherited from `local-certify.mjs` / the vast onstart) **skips the analyze step**. `rollupBundle` drafts verdicts from analyzed subjects, not raw silo artifacts, so with no `analysis.json` beside any subject the rollup is empty and `certify:sign` honestly refuses.

The evidence package already owns the complete chain: `bun run --cwd packages/evidence certify` runs ingest → **analyze** → vision-qa → rollup → reviewer merge → sign → **self-verify**, and exits 0 only when the signed certification self-verifies green. This PR points the hosted workflow at it, with `--skip-matrix` (the documented mode where lane verdicts come from ingested silos — which the deterministic scenario lane step fills on the certified sha) and `--reviewer-kind agent` (this is an automated run; claiming human review would be dishonest).

5b:Td50,Run 31060590880 was the first time the whole certification chain executed end to end — scenario lane, full test matrix, ingest, analysis, rollup, signing — and it produced a **RED certification**: `verdict-failures: 1 failing verdict(s): lane:matrix`. That is the chain working: the matrix failed on the runner, so the signer refused to call the commit green.

The problem: the only record of **why** the matrix failed is `lanes/matrix/log` inside the bundle — and the upload step is skipped when the chain exits non-zero, so the evidence was discarded exactly when it was needed.

Fix: `if: always()` on collect and upload, with the collect step tolerating missing artifacts on early failures (preflight/checkout deaths upload a `NO_BUNDLE.txt` marker instead of nothing). A red certification is a diagnosis, not garbage.

5c:Tfe3,Fifth and (structurally) final fix in the certification-chain series (#17790 → #17792 → #17794 → #17796 → #17797 → this). Run 31059202533 with the orchestrated command:

```text
  matrix: skipped (--skip-matrix)
  analyze: 0 subject(s) at tier full
error [CERTIFICATION_INVALID]: invalid certification payload (payload to sign):
verdicts: Too small: expected array to have >=1 items
```

Reading `rollup.ts` closes the loop: lane verdicts come **exclusively** from bundle paths matching `lanes/<lane>/result.json` (`LANE_RESULT_PATTERN`, rollup.ts:301), and the only writer of those files is the orchestrated **matrix** step, which spawns `packages/scripts/run-all-tests.mjs` and records its outcome. Silo artifacts are evidence attachments, not verdict subjects; visual analysis subjects need screenshots the hosted run does not produce.

So `--skip-matrix` on this runner can never yield a signable certification — and that is the honesty contract saying something true: **a certification is the claim that the repo's test matrix passed on the certified sha.** Run the matrix.

The deterministic scenario lane step stays: its reports ride the bundle as evidence artifacts alongside the matrix verdict.

6f:Tfdc,## What happens

Warm-pool entries whose container has died stay `running` forever, hold their node slot, count against the node's allocation, and make that node permanently undrainable.

Measured on production 2026-08-06 by diffing `docker ps -a` on all nine nodes against the rows that claim them:

| | |
|---|---|
| real agent containers | 169 |
| rows claiming a container | 238 |
| **rows claiming a container that does not exist** | **77** |
| containers with no row at all | 8 (3 up since 13 July) |

Three autoscaled ccx33 nodes bought on 26, 27 and 28 July (`167.233.20.85`, `178.105.77.91`, `88.198.118.204`) hold **four such rows each**, have **zero containers**, and have read as fully allocated for ten days.

## Why nothing collects them

`WarmPoolManager.healthCheck()` probes every ready pool entry and destroys the dead ones — container *and* row, via `destroyPoolContainer` → `deleteAgent` → `deletePoolEntry`. It is exactly the missing collector, and it has **no live caller**: the only one is `/api/v1/cron/pool-health-check` on the container-control-plane, which the daemon's own comments call deprecated. The daemon's `runInfraMaintenanceCycle` runs node-health, disk, alloc-reconcile, pre-pull, autoscale, pool-drain, pool-replenish and orphan-reconcile — no pool health check.

This is the same omission as `replenish`, already documented in `provisioning-worker.ts` fifteen lines away, and nothing else can see these rows:

- **the heartbeat skips them.** `listRunning()` filters `execution_tier != 'shared'`, and `createPoolEntry` never sets `execution_tier`, so every pool row falls to the schema default `shared` — while carrying a real `node_id` and `container_name`. The docblock's premise ("shared rows are container-free by design") is false for pool rows.
- **`reconcileUnclaimable` cannot reach them.** Its candidate query ends `NOT (warmPoolRuntimeReadyConditions)` — a fully ready row is excluded by construction.
- **the orphan reconciler cannot reach them.** It starts from the Docker listing, so an empty node yields an empty candidate set.

## Why it costs servers

- `countAllocatedWorkloadsOnNode` counts non-terminal rows; `running` counts. The node reads as allocated.
- `findDrainCandidates` skips any node with `allocated > 0` — a row is treated as proof of a workload. The node can never be drained.
- `syncAllocatedCounts` runs every five minutes, armed, and re-asserts the inflated count rather than repairing it.
- `container-billing` and `agent-billing` select on `status = 'running'` with no node-side check, so **these rows are billed hourly**.

Net effect: the pool can only grow. Every phantom permanently removes a slot from `totalAvailable` and permanently disqualifies its node from drain.

## Related, not fixed here

- **The 77 rows already stranded** need the reverse reconciler — "row claims container C on node N, `docker ps` does not list it past a grace window → release the placement". No such path exists: every writer of `node_id`/`container_name` to NULL (`executeSleep`, `retireFailedWarmClaimForRetry`, `trySetProvisioning`) is triggered by a job or an error string, never by container absence.
- **`ORPHAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED` is set in no deployment config**, so the container-side reconciler has never run. It would collect the 8 rowless containers. Arming it is an ops decision — it issues `docker rm -f`.
- **`/v1/admin/docker-containers/audit`** — the ghost-container detection route — is a `501` stub.
- **`admin-infrastructure.ts` already computes the drift** and raises a `critical` alert past |2|. The three empty nodes sit at −4, so three critical alerts have been rendering for ten days with no remediation arm.
- **`processDisconnectedRecovery` is scoped `dedicated-always`**, so a `dedicated-lazy` row that flips to `disconnected` is never re-probed and holds its slot permanently — a second, quieter leak.
- **Node `capacity` looks wrong**: the autoscaler buys ccx33 and declares them 4 slots while the original nodes declared 24 are carrying 38.
70:Tbd6,## Problem

`bun run verify` is red on `develop` for every contributor as of `bc3be9cae` (#17812): `audit:hetzner-fleet-routing` throws.

Executed against the actual `develop` workflow tree (extracted via `git archive origin/develop .github/workflows`, validated with the unmodified contract script):

```text
AUDIT FAILS:
Hetzner runner routing must require explicit HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE opt-in; missing, empty, false, and noncanonical values must use a hosted runner:
certification-hosted.yml:33 (on.workflow_dispatch.inputs.runner.description): Runner pool: hosted (ubuntu-24.04) or the self-hosted hetzner-robot fleet
certification-hosted.yml:53 (jobs.hosted-certification.runs-on): ${{ inputs.runner == 'robot' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","hetzner-robot"]') || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
```

Two distinct violations from the same commit:

1. **The `runs-on` selector is non-canonical and skips the `HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE` gate entirely.** `packages/scripts/hetzner-fleet-routing-contract.mjs` allowlists exact selectors, all var-gated, and hard-fails anything else routing to the fleet labels. Beyond the audit, the gap is behavioral: an operator dispatching `runner: robot` while the fleet is offline queues the run against zero registered runners indefinitely — the fail-safe the contract exists to guarantee.
2. **The input's `description` string trips the collector too** — it walks every YAML scalar for the trigger substrings, so the literal `hetzner-robot` in prose is flagged alongside the real selector.

Both were called out pre-merge on #17812 (review thread has the full trace); the merge landed without them.

75:Tbc3,## What happens

`packages/cloud/services/gateway-webhook` cannot be built. Reproduced by running the Dockerfile's own deps step against the service directory:

```
$ bun install --frozen-lockfile --production      # with only package.json, as the Dockerfile does
error: Workspace dependency "@elizaos/cloud-services-common" not found
error: @elizaos/cloud-services-common@workspace:* failed to resolve
```

The Dockerfile builds from the service directory:

```dockerfile
COPY package.json ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --production
```

`workspace:*` has nothing to resolve against in a context that contains only this package.

## When it broke

`a07084e9cbc` (2026-06-28) added `@elizaos/cloud-services-common` to the service's dependencies. Every build since has failed.

Two things hid it:

1. **Nothing builds this service.** It has no repo trigger on Railway (`repoTriggers: NONE`, `source: null`), and `cloud-gateway-webhook.yml` has a single `test` job. The workflow header on the sibling service says *"Railway auto-deploys on push to the watched branch"* — that is not connected for any of these services.
2. **The service ships its own `bun.lock`, and it is stale.** It has no entry for the workspace dependency and pins `hono@4.12.18` while `package.json` asks for `4.12.34`. The root lockfile has both right. So `--frozen-lockfile` was reading a lockfile written before the dependency existed.

## What it cost

The production image dates from **2026-05-14** — the last build that could succeed. Everything since is a redeploy of that image. The running container still logs the pre-#17746 error string, which is how this was found:

```
[ERRO] Background message processing failed
       error="Identity resolve response missing userId, organizationId, or agentId"
```

So #17746 and #17764 — both merged, both fixing connector onboarding for every linked user — have never run in production. Nothing reported this: tests, typecheck and lint all pass, because none of them builds the image.

## Scope: this is a class, not one service

| service | workspace deps | last successful build |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway-webhook` | 1 | 2026-05-14 |
| `gateway-discord` | 1 | 2026-06-19 |
| `agent-server` | 6 | 2026-05-15 |

All three have the same `COPY package.json ./` shape. `gateway-discord` also carries a stale local lockfile.

## Fix

Build from the repository root and write a pruned workspace root in the deps stage — only the service and the packages it needs — so the workspace link resolves without installing the whole monorepo. Measured: 32 packages, 1.5s.

Guarded by a test that derives, for every service with a `workspace:*` dependency, whether its Dockerfile copies that package. The two services still broken are listed explicitly rather than skipped, so fixing one fails the test until the list is updated.

Not covered here: nothing yet guards the deploy half — a service can still go months without a successful build and no signal. Worth a separate check.
76:T8a5,## What happens

Meta cannot register the WhatsApp callback URL. Measured against production on 2026-08-05:

```
GET https://api.elizacloud.ai/api/eliza-app/webhook/whatsapp?hub.mode=subscribe&hub.verify_token=<token>&hub.challenge=PROBE123
→ 401 {"success":false,"code":"WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID","error":"Invalid webhook signature"}
```

Expected is `200` with the body `PROBE123`.

## Why

Meta verifies a callback URL with a `GET` carrying `hub.mode=subscribe`, `hub.verify_token` and `hub.challenge`, **and no signature header** — there is no body to sign. That is the documented handshake.

`forwardToWebhookGateway` runs `validateLocalWebhookSignature` on every request regardless of method. For a GET, `needsBody` is false, so the body is `""`, and `verifyWhatsAppSignature` returns `false` the moment `x-hub-signature-256` is absent. Meta's challenge is refused before it is read.

The gateway on the other side already implements the handshake correctly — `GET /webhook/:project/whatsapp[/:agentId]` compares `hub.verify_token` and echoes `hub.challenge` — but Meta hits the Worker URL, so it never gets there.

## Why it matters beyond WhatsApp

There are two independent WhatsApp failures in production and they have a mandatory order. The access token has been expired since 2026-02-09 (`Session has expired on Monday, 09-Feb-26 09:00:00 PST`), but regenerating it changes nothing while the URL cannot be registered. This bug is first.

Current state: `SELECT count(*) FROM user_identities WHERE whatsapp_id IS NOT NULL` → **0**. No WhatsApp user has ever existed.

## Fix

Skip the body-signature check for exactly that handshake — WhatsApp platform, `GET`, `hub.mode=subscribe`, `hub.challenge` present — and let it proxy to the gateway, which validates the verify token. The HMAC check on an empty body proves nothing; the verify token is the credential Meta's design uses for this step. Every other WhatsApp request, including every POST, keeps the signature requirement.

## Related

The same audit found that Twilio and blooio share the symptom (`phone_message_log` empty since forever) but their configuration lives with other providers and has not been audited. Separate work.

7e:Ta81,## Problem

`MainActivity.onCreate()` unconditionally calls
`ElizaWorkScheduler.enqueuePeriodic()`. On a real LP3 using the
paired-LAN/remote runtime, Capacitor Preferences has no
`eliza:device-secret`, so `ElizaTasksWorker` wakes every 15 minutes and returns
`Result.failure()` before it can deliver `/api/internal/wake`.

Physical-device log evidence on 2026-08-06:

```text
15:15:19.624 WM-WorkerWrapper: Starting work for ai.elizaos.app.ElizaTasksWorker
15:15:19.625 ElizaTasksWorker: device secret not provisioned; skipping wake (permanent failure until JS writes it)
15:15:19.628 WM-WorkerWrapper: Worker result FAILURE
15:30:19.654 WM-WorkerWrapper: Starting work for ai.elizaos.app.ElizaTasksWorker
15:30:19.654 ElizaTasksWorker: device secret not provisioned; skipping wake (permanent failure until JS writes it)
15:30:19.658 WM-WorkerWrapper: Worker result FAILURE
```

This did **not** crash or restart the app; Android `ApplicationExitInfo` shows
only development APK replacements and explicit force-stops today. It is still
unnecessary work, noisy diagnostics, and a broken ownership contract.

The boot receiver already checks `eliza:background-enabled`, but
`MainActivity` does not. Neither `eliza:device-secret` nor
`eliza:agent-base` is part of the current native storage sync set, so the
schedule can be present with no deliverable target.

## Correct boundary

Periodic wake work should be reconciled from the selected runtime and
background preference, not blindly enqueued. A remote paired runtime with no
native wake credentials must have no scheduled phone-local wake. A committed
local/hybrid runtime should schedule only after the wake credential/target is
actually provisioned. Disabling background work or changing away from an owned
target should cancel the unique work.

Do not convert the worker's missing-credential failure into fake success and do
not add an aggressive retry/watchdog.

## Acceptance criteria

- MainActivity and boot/package-replace paths use one idempotent schedule/cancel authority.
- The authority requires background enabled plus a valid wake target/credential owned by the selected runtime.
- Remote paired mode with no credentials leaves no `ElizaTasksWorker` JobScheduler entry and emits no 15-minute failure.
- Local/hybrid mode with valid credentials still delivers a real authenticated `/api/internal/wake`.
- Switching modes or disabling background cancels stale unique work; provisioning a valid target schedules it.
- Focused unit/source-generation tests cover schedule, cancel, missing-secret, local, hybrid, and remote cases.
- Real Android evidence includes `dumpsys jobscheduler`, worker logs, and no app process restart.
7f:T25ad,## Summary

Productionize the BlueBubbles → Eliza Cloud phone gateway on a dedicated Mac and make self-message loops impossible by construction.

A live same-Apple-Account test exposed two coupled failures:

1. A Mac signed into personal and gateway Messages identities allowed unrelated personal traffic to reach the relay.
2. Sending from the gateway number to itself produced alternating BlueBubbles copies (`isFromMe: true` and `isFromMe: false`) whose sender and receiving identity were both the gateway. The relay treated the false copy as new inbound traffic, sent the agent reply back to the gateway, and repeated until the relay was stopped.

The launchd process also received `SQLITE_AUTH` when trying to read `~/Library/Messages/chat.db`. Safety decisions must not depend on direct Messages DB access or Full Disk Access.

This issue covers the dedicated-Mac deployment runbook, an idempotent installer, sender/account linking, private-API readiness, loop prevention, and real end-to-end proof.

## Security model

This deployment intentionally disables SIP for the BlueBubbles private API. It must run on a dedicated gateway Mac only:

- No personal Apple Account, phone number, email identity, Messages history, or daily-driver data.
- Use a dedicated macOS user and dedicated Apple Account for the gateway number.
- Enable FileVault, automatic security updates, and the host firewall.
- Bind BlueBubbles to localhost/LAN as narrowly as practical; do not expose its password or local API directly to the public Internet.
- Store relay secrets in a mode-`0600` file and never print them in logs, screenshots, issues, or CI.
- Keep BlueBubbles and the relay local-only; Cloud remains the authenticated public boundary.
- Disabling SIP is a human-owned recovery-mode step and must be documented with the associated security tradeoff.

## Required behavior

### Identity isolation

- Subscribe only to BlueBubbles `new-message` events.
- Before contacting Cloud, retrieve the full message through the authenticated local BlueBubbles API and verify `chats[].lastAddressedHandle === BLUEBUBBLES_GATEWAY_PHONE_NUMBER`.
- Fail closed when the receiving identity is absent, cannot be retrieved, or differs from the configured gateway.
- Reject every `isFromMe: true` event.
- Reject every inbound event whose sender/peer normalizes to the gateway number (`gateway_self_message`).
- Refuse every outbound send whose derived recipient normalizes to the gateway number.
- Do not use a configured fallback identity to reinterpret an uncertain `isFromMe` event.
- Never depend on `chat.db` access for a safety decision.

The relevant implementation is `packages/cloud/scripts/bluebubbles-local-bridge.ts`; regression coverage belongs in `packages/cloud/scripts/bluebubbles-local-bridge.registered-e2e.test.ts`.

### User/agent routing

The gateway is sender-owned:

- An E.164 sender identity resolves to that sender's signed-in Eliza Cloud user.
- The signed-in connectors flow must verify/link the phone identity to the intended Cloud account.
- Exactly one non-gateway running sandbox should be selected for that owner.
- An unknown sender receives the secure sign-in/onboarding continuation.
- A known user without an agent receives provisioning/onboarding state, never a fabricated agent response.
- A stopped agent, insufficient credits, ambiguous agents, and login/link failures are explicit states.
- Once the user signs in, the next message must route to their agent without retaining a stale negative lookup.

The UI must make the current phone-to-account-to-agent binding visible and revocable.

### 1. Base system

81:Tee7,## Summary

On `develop@35f634551`, a repository-layer app mutation evicts the worker-lifetime memory cache **without advancing the hydration generation**. An authoritative read that started before the mutation therefore resumes afterwards, fails to notice the invalidation, and republishes the pre-mutation row into the **shared** cache — where every worker serves it for the full `CacheTTL.app.byId`.

This is a regression in behavior relative to the service-layer invalidation path, which has always advanced the generation.

## The two halves that came apart

`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/inference-app-memory-cache.ts` only deletes:

```ts
export function evictInferenceAppMemoryCache(appId: string): void {
  inferenceAppMemoryCache.delete(appId);
}
```

`appByIdHydrationGeneration` stays private to `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/apps.ts:22`, where `invalidateCache` still bumps it (`:342`) and `loadAndCacheAppById` samples it across the DB round trip (`:165`, `:167`).

The repository calls the evictor that does *not* bump — `packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/apps.ts:36`, reached from `invalidateAppCacheEntries` at `:480`, `:496`, `:498`, each awaited after the write commits.

## Interleaving

1. A read enters `loadAndCacheAppById(id)`, samples `generation = 0`, and awaits `appsRepository.findById(id)`, which returns the pre-mutation row **R**.
2. A mutation commits and calls `invalidateAppCacheEntries` → `evictInferenceAppMemoryCache(id)` plus the `cache.del`s. The generation is still `0`.
3. The read resumes. `0 !== 0` is false, so it publishes:
   - `await cache.set(cacheKey, R, CacheTTL.app.byId)` — stale row into the **shared** cache
   - `inferenceAppMemoryCache.set(id, R)` — stale row back into the cache just evicted

## Why it matters

The pre-fix bug this evictor was added for stranded a stale row in one worker's memory for the 30s LRU TTL. In this interleaving the outcome is worse: the row is republished into the shared cache, so the staleness escapes the worker and is served cluster-wide for the full shared TTL.

It is also not a rare interleaving — `scheduleAppByIdHydration` deliberately runs hydrations in the background under `waitUntil`, so reads overlapping a mutation are the steady state rather than a corner case.

## Reproduction

Parking an authoritative read inside `findById`, invalidating through the repository primitive, then releasing the read:

```text
(fail) AppsService inference cache-only lookup > an invalidation racing an in-flight read is not undone by that read
  expect(inferenceAppMemoryCache.get(row.id)).toBeNull()
  Received: { id: "app-1", ... monetization_enabled: true }
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `evictInferenceAppMemoryCache` deletes the entry **and** advances the hydration generation, so the repository path and the service path invalidate identically.
- [ ] The generation lives alongside the cache it guards, rather than in the service, so a caller cannot evict without bumping.
- [ ] `loadAndCacheAppById` reads the generation through the shared accessor.
- [ ] A regression test parks a read mid-`findById`, invalidates, and asserts the read does not republish into either cache — failing on the current `develop` behavior.
- [ ] No change to the default lane's cache TTLs or read paths.

82:T1de0,## Summary

Following the contribution skill exactly — fill the repository template's
`contribution-attribution` rows, then append the eliza.army footer — produces a PR
body whose **machine marker is rejected by the scoring validator**. The
declaration that carries `client` and `skill_revision` is dropped, and the PR is
credited only with the weaker visible declarations (both `client: null`,
`skillRevision: null`). Coverage falls from `complete` to `partial`.

Both gates are individually satisfied. It is their combination — which the skill
instructs and CI enforces — that fails.

## Mechanism

`src/lib/leaderboard.ts` (elizaOS/army@`753f8446`, the deployed validator) counts
attribution footer lines across the **whole body**:

```ts
const providerModelLines  = attributionLineValues(body, "AI provider/model");
const clientLines         = attributionLineValues(body, "Client / agent tooling");
const skillRevisionLines  = attributionLineValues(body, "(?:Contribution skill revision|Skill revision)");
const statusLines         = attributionLineValues(body, "Attribution status");
if (providerModelLines.length !== 1 || clientLines.length !== 1 ||
    skillRevisionLines.length !== 1 || statusLines.length !== 1) {
  return "marker requires exactly one complete visible attribution footer";
}
```

`.github/pull_request_template.md` (develop, lines 32–37) ships three of those
four label texts as **mandatory** rows:

```
<!-- attribution-row:client -->
- Client / agent tooling: `client-name` / `None - human-only contribution`
<!-- attribution-row:skill-revision -->
- Skill revision: `owner/repo@full-commit-sha:path` / `N/A - no contribution skill used`
<!-- attribution-row:status -->
- Attribution status: `self-reported`
```

`scripts/check-pr-agent-attribution.mjs` requires every one of
`REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTION_ROWS = [ai-assistance, models, client, skill-revision, status]`
to be present with a concrete value, so the rows cannot simply be deleted — that
turns the PR gate red. And the skill states the rule that pairs them:

> fill the contribution-attribution row in the repository template and append
> this footer after the template.

Filling the template puts `Client / agent tooling:`, `Skill revision:` and
`Attribution status:` in the body; appending the footer puts
`Client / agent tooling:`, `Contribution skill revision:` and `Attribution
status:` in it again. Each count is 2, the marker is rejected, and the strong
declaration is lost.

The issue templates already carry the instruction that avoids this.
`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md` tells reporters to add the marker as the
final body lines and **"Do not repeat the visible rows."** No such sentence
exists in `.github/pull_request_template.md`, and the skill's PR instruction says
the opposite — fill the template row *and* append the footer.

## Every arrangement was measured

Same PR body, four variants, all with the repository CI gate green
(`evaluatePrAttribution(body).findings === []`):

| PR body | scorer verdict |
| --- | --- |
| template rows + full footer (what the skill instructs) | `marker requires exactly one complete visible attribution footer` — partial |
| template rows + lane signature + marker (the issue template's rule, applied to a PR) | same reason — partial |
| template rows + marker only | `marker requires exactly one terminal lane signature` — partial |
| template rows with **relabelled** rows + full footer | `machine-marker`, client captured, **complete** |
| template provenance block deleted + full footer | `machine-marker`, complete — but the CI gate then fails |

So on the PR side there is no arrangement that follows the template's own label
text and keeps the marker valid. The only shapes that work either deviate from
the template's wording or drop rows CI requires.

## Reproduction

Against the shipped code on both sides, no reimplementation:

```
$ gh pr view 17749 --repo elizaOS/eliza --json body --jq .body > body.md
# scoring validator, imported from elizaOS/army@753f8446:src/lib/leaderboard.ts
assessModelAttribution([{ id: "PR:body", kind: "body", body, ... }])

declarations : ["visible-declaration", "visible-declaration"]   # client: null, null
invalidMarkers: ["marker requires exactly one complete visible attribution footer"]
coverage     : "partial"

# repository CI gate, imported from elizaOS/eliza@develop:scripts/check-pr-agent-attribution.mjs
evaluatePrAttribution(body).findings -> []      # PASSES
```

Deleting only the template's provenance block from the same body flips the
scorer to `machine-marker`, `client: "Claude Code"`, `invalidMarkers: []`,
`coverage: "complete"` — and would fail the CI gate.

The same verdict is produced by the previously deployed validator
(elizaOS/army@`04a50cb0`), so this is not a recent regression; it has been
dropping markers for as long as both requirements have coexisted.

## Blast radius

Every AI-assisted PR to this repository that follows the skill and the template.
The lost fields are exactly the ones the ledger uses to attribute a contribution
to a client and a skill revision, so the effect is silent: the PR still shows a
visible declaration, CI is green, and nothing reports that the marker was
discarded.

## Candidate fixes

1. **Scope the count to the footer block (preferred, validator-side).**
   `markerFooterError` already isolates the terminal footer — it locates the
   marker, walks back over the declaration lines, and requires exactly one
   terminal lane signature immediately before the marker. Counting the four
   labels within that block instead of the whole body preserves every property
   the check enforces (a complete footer, adjacent to its marker, matching the
   marker payload) while ignoring rows elsewhere in the body. Note this file
   lives in `elizaOS/army`, not here.

2. **Relabel the template rows (contributor-side workaround, no validator
   change).** `rowValue()` in `check-pr-agent-attribution.mjs` strips a leading
   `- ` and then `^[^:]+:\s*`, so a row's visible label is not load-bearing for
   the CI gate — only its `<!-- attribution-row:… -->` marker and its value are.
   Rewording the three colliding labels (for example `Agent tooling:`,
   `Skill ref:`, `Disclosure:`) satisfies both gates today: measured on the same
   body, CI findings `[]` and scorer `machine-marker` / `coverage: complete`.
   The skill-revision row must keep *some* label ending in a colon, because
   `rowValue` would otherwise strip everything up to the first colon of
   `owner/repo@sha:path` and mangle the value.

Fix 1 is the right shape — the template's labels are the natural English for
those rows, and a contributor should not have to know which words a downstream
parser reserves. Fix 2 is offered because it is available immediately and needs
nothing from the scoring repository.

I'm happy to open either PR (or both) — say which, and whether the template
change should preserve the current labels in a comment for readers.

This issue body deliberately carries a single attribution footer and no template
provenance rows, because that is the only shape that currently keeps its own
marker valid.

83:T828,## Problem

The current Mac voice path has three independently reproduced boundary failures:

1. The TypeScript FFI binding requires ABI v15, while `develop` still pins the native `llama.cpp` submodule at an ABI v14 revision. The official real-ASR smoke fails closed on that mismatch.
2. Gemma4 turn markers may tokenize as the paired `<|turn>` / `<turn|>` contract rather than the legacy single token expected by the semantic end-of-turn scorer.
3. `voice:interactive --wav` decodes WAV bytes to normalized `Float32Array` PCM and then reinterprets those Float32 bytes as PCM16, corrupting the signal. Its fixed sleep also allows false-positive completion.

These failures can make local text-to-speech appear healthy while the real mic/WAV VAD → ASR → agent → TTS path never completes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publish/review the native ABI v15 Kokoro/OmniVoice implementation and update the main-repo submodule pointer to that reviewed revision.
- [ ] Preserve both Gemma4 paired-turn and legacy end-of-turn token contracts with focused scorer coverage.
- [ ] Feed decoded Float32 WAV PCM exactly once, paced at capture cadence.
- [ ] Make one-shot voice QA terminate only on a real completed turn, explicit suppression, timeout, or error.
- [ ] Keep the engine-owned VAD lifecycle private; the harness must not reach into private VAD state.
- [ ] Pass package typecheck/tests, full repository build/verify, and the official real-ASR smoke.
- [ ] Capture and manually review a real Mac VAD → ASR → agent → audible TTS run, including the output WAV and terminal envelope.
- [ ] Do not claim LP3/cloud readiness from the Mac proof; those environments retain their own deployment/evidence gates.

## Reproduction evidence

- ABI mismatch: binding expects v15; pinned native library reports v14.
- With the reviewed ABI15 native branch, the official ASR smoke produces a real transcript in about one second.
- With the decoded-PCM and terminal-completion repair, the combined real path reaches VAD → ASR → agent reply → TTS and writes a valid 24 kHz mono PCM16 WAV.

# What changed

- Persists voice turns in canonical chat history, clears the composer after send, and keeps reconnect/resync state coherent.
- Keeps automatic TTS state in the composer waveform/Stop control and prevents message-action flashes.
- Prevents local runtime mode from booting an unrelated on-device text model.
- Preserves the mounted shell during background auth revalidation instead of flashing onboarding and rebuilding native listeners.

# Root cause

The provider gateway and visible composer had separate owners. The realtime hook was mounted in `ChatView`, but the product surface renders `ChatOverlay`, whose Talk control still invoked batch Cloud ASR. Message playback status also forced the action rail visible before Motion applied its hidden state.

For the LP3 notification regression, `HomeScreen` capped the list at an arbitrary 40% of a short viewport while the adjacent launcher region retained unused space. The shared scroll-fade fallback masked both edges unconditionally in WebViews, including the top edge at scroll start and lists with no hidden content.

Transcript and response remain in the same conversation, TTS is interruptible, there is no duplicate mic, and fast turns do not flash message controls. On LP3-size screens the full available notification area is used and fades identify only content beyond the current scroll edge.

89:T1e25,> **Draft.** Backend, security, and behaviour work is complete and green, and the CI availability regression is fixed: fail-closed is now scoped to bridge-issued tokens (stamped with a `bridged: true` claim at /exchange re-mint), so ordinary session sync performs no datastore read at all - the pre-existing Redis-outage test passes unmodified, and a new suite proves a bridged token fails closed (503 `sso_unavailable`) during a marker-store outage. Remaining before undraft: the three surface-artifact rows (screenshots + walkthrough of the cross-origin flow), which need two live origins and are not faked here.

Security review of the dashboard/app SSO bridge found the single-use guarantee did not hold on the deployed cache and the logout marker failed open. This reworks the bridge onto a store that can actually deliver both, and closes four further findings.

## F1 (HIGH) — single-use codes were not atomic in production

The bridge claimed single-use via `cache.getAndDelete`, which on Cloudflare KV is a read-then-delete, not an atomic claim. `supportsAtomicOperations()` was never consulted, and the suite passed only because the mock was an atomic in-memory map. Two concurrent presenters of the same code could both be issued a session.

Codes now live in Postgres (`sso_bridge_codes`) and consumption is a single statement:

```sql
DELETE FROM sso_bridge_codes
 WHERE code_hash = $1 AND expires_at > now()
 RETURNING claims, challenge_hash
```

Exactly one of N concurrent presenters gets the row. Insert collision is a primary-key violation, so minting is atomically NX. Rows store `sha256(code)`, `sha256(verifier)`, and the **verified claims** — never a session JWT at rest; `/exchange` re-mints a fresh token from those claims, capped to the original token's `exp`.

This holds because KV is no longer in the path at all — the claim runs on the Worker's strongly-consistent Hyperdrive Postgres, the same store that already backs sessions and idempotency fences.

## F2 (HIGH) — logout marker failed open, and was invisible for ~60s

The marker was a cache key: a KV read miss during an outage read as "not logged out", and KV's propagation window meant a real logout stayed invisible to the paired origin. Both failure modes bridged a session that should have been dead.

The marker moves to Postgres (upsert with `GREATEST`, so it only moves forward). `isBlockedBySsoBridgeLogout` now **throws** on store failure and both bridge legs translate that into `503 sso_unavailable`, so the client falls back to per-origin login. An outage means no bridging — never "not logged out". Because codes and markers share one store, an outage that could lose a stamp also disables minting entirely.

## F3 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — dashboard sign-out never stamped, and the paired origin re-planted cookies

Three parts: both `ConsoleShell` sign-out branches now route through `signOutFromSsoBridgedHost`; `POST /api/auth/steward-session` refuses tokens issued at or before the marker with a distinct `401 session_ended`, killing the cookie re-plant server-side; and `StewardProviderRuntime` treats `session_ended` as a real revocation rather than a stale-proxy blip.

**Residual, documented in code:** the paired origin's raw bearer still works against the API until `exp`. Closing that needs a revocation lookup inside `verifyStewardTokenCached`, which is platform-wide and out of this PR's scope.

## F4/F5/F8 — binding and abuse surface

- **PKCE binding**: the app origin generates a verifier (sessionStorage only); `sha256(verifier)` travels as `challenge`. `/mint` requires it, `/exchange` requires the verifier. HTTP logs and history no longer contain enough to redeem a code.
- **Claim-then-verify**: the server consumes before checking the verifier, so every refusal path burns the code; the client also fires a verifier-less burn on state-mismatch. The mint leg requires `document.referrer` to be the paired origin, so a forced cross-site navigation cannot drive minting.
- **Origin gate**: the `Referer` fallback is removed — Origin-only, fail closed.

**F6** (plantable `steward-authed` hint) is documented as accepted risk: it is a routing hint only, loop-guarded to one bounce per tab per 5 minutes, and no unplantable cross-origin signal exists for a first visit. **F7** (logout CSRF) is pre-existing and flagged as follow-up.

## Migration

`0188_sso_bridge_store.sql` is hand-written, matching 0082–0187 in this repo (no drizzle snapshots since 0081).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This collapses the current GitHub Actions surface from 121 workflow files to 17 and removes 104 redundant workflows plus their orphaned scripts, tests, composite actions, and stale documentation.

The resulting model is:

- one pull-request workflow: `CI`
- one stable branch-protection context: `CI / Required`
- nightly reuse of the same CI contract, plus macOS and Windows smoke checks
- manual-only live integration, infrastructure, certification, and release operations
- path-scoped deployment and image workflows after merge
- one scheduled maintenance workflow

The PR workflow classifies changes, runs repository quality, affected tests, a focused deterministic core-shell browser smoke, and a diff-scoped secret scan. Individual diagnostic jobs remain visible but branch protection needs only the stable aggregate.

## What kind of change is this?

Infrastructure and CI simplification with narrow reliability fixes discovered while exercising the new lanes.
